notes: Web searches: ~58 WebSearch calls plus ~45 AISC directory name queries and ~25 page fetches. Registries mined: TxDOT (ITS, high mast, roadway-illumination, traffic-signal lists), Georgia QPL-52, Maryland signal structures, Massachusetts approved fabricators, Ohio signal supports, Wisconsin sign structures, Iowa 2013 list, Caltrans steel standards and poles, SCDOT QPL-95, AISC (names containing pole, tower, structures, utility, sign, traffic, valmont, meyer, arcosa, sabre and ~40 company names). The AISC search box is name-contains; the Highway Component Manufacturer filter was not used directly. Confidence is high where own site or release was fetched, low where only a registry row or a search summary supports the item. Quotes for registry entries are whitespace-collapsed registry rows and show existence/location, not product line; product claims for those come from other listed sources in the note. Items with an empty quote were seen only in search summaries and need a fetch before use. Not searched state by state for all 50 states; coverage is by registry plus regional queries (TX, OK, KS, MO, MN/WI/IA, OH/PA/NY/CT/NJ, LA/AL/MS/AR/TN/KY, WA/OR/UT/AZ, NC/SC/VA, NE/Dakotas/MT/WY/ID, MI/IL/IN). No steel pole plant found for Mississippi, Dakotas, Montana, Wyoming, Idaho, Nevada, New Mexico, New England beyond CT. Not checked: Pennsylvania Bulletin 15 database, NYSDOT, FDOT APL and NCDOT lists (not reachable by search), Michigan MDOT. Dropped as out of scope: lattice-only (Stella-Jones lattice TN, Rohn), concrete/composite (Valmont Tuscaloosa/Bartow, Resilient Structures, RS, Avient), wood (Koppers), galvanizers, Kubes Steel (Canada), Trylon and Nova Pole (Canada), Access Fixtures and LSI (distributors/unclear). Valmont Claremore OK and El Dorado KS AISC rows are Building Fabricator only and were not included. Meyer Memphis is HQ, not a confirmed plant.
